"""Checks relative links and anchors in Markdown files.

Usage: scripts/check-md-links.py FILE.md [FILE.md ...]

For every [text](target) and <a href="target"> in the given files, outside
code blocks and inline code: the target file must exist in the repository,
and a #fragment must match a heading (GitHub's slug rules, duplicates
numbered) or an explicit id/name anchor in the target Markdown file.
External links (http:, https:, mailto:, ...) are not checked. Exits 1 if
any link is broken.
"""
import html
import pathlib
import re
import sys
import urllib.parse

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def strip_code(text):
    """Blank out fenced code blocks and inline code, keeping line numbers."""
    out, fence = [], None
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"^\s*(```+|~~~+)", line)
        if fence:
            if m and m.group(1)[0] == fence[0] and len(m.group(1)) >= len(fence):
                fence = None
            out.append("")
            continue
        if m:
            fence = m.group(1)
            out.append("")
            continue
        out.append(re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "``", line))
    return out


def slug(heading):
    text = re.sub(r"`([^`]*)`", r"\1", heading)
    text = re.sub(r"!?\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text)
    text = html.unescape(text).strip().lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", text)
    return text.replace(" ", "-")


_anchors = {}


def anchors(path):
    if path not in _anchors:
        found, seen, fence = set(), {}, None
        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            m = re.match(r"^\s*(```+|~~~+)", line)
            if fence:
                if m and m.group(1)[0] == fence[0] and len(m.group(1)) >= len(fence):
                    fence = None
                continue
            if m:
                fence = m.group(1)
                continue
            h = re.match(r"^#{1,6}\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$", line)
            if h:
                s = slug(h.group(1))
                n = seen.get(s, 0)
                seen[s] = n + 1
                found.add(s if n == 0 else f"{s}-{n}")
            for a in re.findall(r'<a\s+(?:id|name)="([^"]+)"', line):
                found.add(a)
        _anchors[path] = found
    return _anchors[path]


LINK = re.compile(r"\]\(\s*<?([^)\s>]+)>?(?:\s+\"[^\"]*\")?\s*\)|href=\"([^\"]+)\"")


def check(md):
    errors = []
    for no, line in enumerate(strip_code(md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), 1):
        for m in LINK.finditer(line):
            url = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
            if re.match(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:", url, re.I) or url.startswith("//"):
                continue
            target, _, frag = url.partition("#")
            frag = urllib.parse.unquote(frag)
            path = (md.parent / urllib.parse.unquote(target)).resolve() if target else md
            if not path.exists():
                errors.append(f"{md.relative_to(ROOT)}:{no}: missing file: {url}")
                continue
            if frag and path.suffix == ".md" and frag not in anchors(path):
                errors.append(f"{md.relative_to(ROOT)}:{no}: missing anchor: {url}")
    return errors


def main(args):
    if not args:
        print(__doc__.strip().splitlines()[2], file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    errors = []
    for a in args:
        errors += check(pathlib.Path(a).resolve())
    for e in errors:
        print(e)
    print(f"{len(args)} files, {len(errors)} broken links", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1 if errors else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

                ORDER.get(v.get("Severity", "UNKNOWN"), 4),
                name,
                result.get("Target", ""),
                v.get("VulnerabilityID", ""),
                v.get("PkgName", ""),
                v.get("InstalledVersion", ""),
                v.get("FixedVersion", "") or "no fix yet",
                v.get("Severity", "UNKNOWN"),
            )


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) < 3:
        print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    title, paths = argv[1], argv[2:]
    found = sorted({r for p in paths for r in rows(p)})
    print(f"## {title}\n")
    if not found:
        print("No known vulnerabilities.")
        return 0
    fixable = sum(1 for r in found if r[6] != "no fix yet")
    print(f"{len(found)} known vulnerabilities, {fixable} with a fixed version. "
          "Fix them with a patch release (SECURITY.md: Critical within 48 hours, High within 7 days), "
          "or record why one does not apply in `.vex/guard-spec.openvex.json`.\n")
    print("| Image | Target | ID | Package | Installed | Fixed | Severity |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for _, image, target, vid, pkg, inst, fixed, sev in found[:MAX_ROWS]:
        print(f"| {image} | {target} | {vid} | {pkg} | {inst} | {fixed} | {sev} |")
    if len(found) > MAX_ROWS:
        print(f"\n{len(found) - MAX_ROWS} more of the lowest severities left out; the workflow run has the full reports.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

"""A fake OpenAI-compatible model for running the examples without a real one.

It serves POST /v1/chat/completions (plain and streamed), POST /v1/completions
and GET /v1/models with the Python standard library only. Its answer
describes what it received, so the examples can show what reached the model
through Guard Spec: the last user message, and the content of every tool
result (a retrieved document, or Guard Spec's placeholder when it was
redacted).

    python3 examples/dev/fake_upstream.py --port 18199

Then start the gateway with UPSTREAM_LLM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18199/v1.
Not a model: never point anything but these examples at it.
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer


def text_of(content):
    """The text of a message's content (a string or a list of parts)."""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        return " ".join(p.get("text", "") for p in content if isinstance(p, dict))
    return ""


def answer(messages):
    tool_results = [text_of(m.get("content")) for m in messages if m.get("role") == "tool"]
    users = [text_of(m.get("content")) for m in messages if m.get("role") == "user"]
    if tool_results:
        shown = "; ".join(f"[{t[:100]}]" for t in tool_results)
        return f"(fake model) I read {len(tool_results)} document(s): {shown}"
    return f"(fake model) You said: {users[-1] if users else ''}"


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # quiet
        pass

    def send_json(self, status, body):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path.rstrip("/") in ("/v1/models", "/models"):
            self.send_json(200, {"object": "list", "data": [
                {"id": "fake-model", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "examples"}]})
        else:
            self.send_json(404, {"error": {"message": "not found"}})

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        try:
            req = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            self.send_json(400, {"error": {"message": "invalid JSON"}})
            return
        model = req.get("model", "fake-model")
        path = self.path.rstrip("/")
        if path.endswith("/chat/completions"):
            text = answer(req.get("messages") or [])
        elif path.endswith("/completions"):
            text = f"(fake model) You said: {text_of(req.get('prompt'))}"
            self.send_json(200, {"id": "cmpl-fake", "object": "text_completion", "created": int(time.time()),
                                 "model": model, "choices": [{"index": 0, "text": text, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
                                 "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2}})
            return
        else:
            self.send_json(404, {"error": {"message": "not found"}})
            return

        created = int(time.time())
        usage = {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": len(text.split()), "total_tokens": 10 + len(text.split())}
        if not req.get("stream"):
            self.send_json(200, {"id": "chatcmpl-fake", "object": "chat.completion", "created": created,
                                 "model": model, "usage": usage,
                                 "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                                              "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": text}}]})
            return

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()
        self.close_connection = True

        def event(delta, finish=None, with_usage=False):
            chunk = {"id": "chatcmpl-fake", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": created, "model": model,
                     "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": delta, "finish_reason": finish}]}
            if with_usage:
                chunk["usage"] = usage
            self.wfile.write(b"data: " + json.dumps(chunk).encode() + b"\n\n")
            self.wfile.flush()

        event({"role": "assistant", "content": ""})
        words = text.split(" ")
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            event({"content": word + (" " if i < len(words) - 1 else "")})
        event({}, "stop", with_usage=True)
        self.wfile.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
        self.wfile.flush()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18199)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((args.host, args.port), Handler)
    print(f"fake upstream on http://{args.host}:{args.port}/v1", flush=True)
    server.serve_forever()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ==> docker-compose.yml <==
# Secrets have no defaults here. Production: copy .env.example to .env, fill it
# in, and run `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d` (so that the dev
# override is not loaded). The services refuse to start with missing, default
# or weak secrets unless GUARD_ENV=dev, which docker-compose.override.yml sets.

#
# Images: the released ones from ghcr.io (GUARDSPEC_VERSION picks the tag).
# Contributors build from source instead: `docker compose up --build` also
# loads docker-compose.override.yml, which adds the build sections (and
# GUARD_ENV=dev). On a clean machine, scripts/quickstart.sh writes a .env
# with strong secrets and starts this file alone.
#
# Models: the models-init service pulls the recommended models of
# models/manifest.yaml into ./models/cache/<name>/<version>/ before the
# gateway starts, verifying every SHA-256 (docs/models.md). It does nothing
# when they are already there.

# Default project name; -p or COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME override it.
name: guard-spec

services:
  gateway:
    image: ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:${GUARDSPEC_VERSION:-0.4.1}
    ports:
      - "${GATEWAY_PORT:-8080}:8080"   # proxy API (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Messages)
      - "${METRICS_PORT:-9090}:9090"   # Prometheus metrics
    environment:
      GUARD_ENV: ${GUARD_ENV:-}
      # The password comes from PGPASSWORD so that it is never part of a URL here.
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://guardspec_app@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-guardspec}?sslmode=disable
      PGPASSWORD: ${GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD:-}
      # Audit rows keep hashes and lengths only; true also stores the content.
      AUDIT_STORE_CONTENT: ${AUDIT_STORE_CONTENT:-false}
      # Encrypts stored content (with AUDIT_STORE_CONTENT or an org's opt-in):
      # 32 random bytes, base64 (openssl rand -base64 32), the same on the
      # gateway and the control plane. Back it up: without it stored content
      # cannot be read. Vault Transit instead: docs/security/README.md#encryption.
      CONTENT_KEK: ${CONTENT_KEK:-}

text:
# SHA256SUMS for the files that matched, signs it with cosign keyless (GitHub
# OIDC, no long-lived key) and attaches SHA256SUMS and
# SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json to the release. A file that does not match its pin
# fails the run and nothing is signed. Run it again after replacing a file.
#
# This is a signature, not build provenance: the model is trained outside
# GitHub Actions, so no workflow can honestly claim to have built it. Verify:
# docs/security/verifying-releases.md.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Model version (release tag model-guardspec-classifier-<version>)
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  sign:
    # The signing identity names the ref; verification pins refs/heads/main.
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write   # attach the signature to the release
      id-token: write   # cosign keyless signing through GitHub OIDC
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - name: Download and check against models/manifest.yaml
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          case "$VERSION" in ""|*[!a-z0-9.-]*) echo "::error::bad version: $VERSION"; exit 1 ;; esac
          dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/m/guardspec-classifier/$VERSION"
          gh release download "model-guardspec-classifier-$VERSION" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -D "$dir"
          go run ./cmd/models verify -dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/m" "guardspec-classifier@$VERSION" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/verify.txt"
          # Only the files the manifest pins and that matched ("<path>: ok").
          sed -n 's|^.*/\([^/]*\): ok$|\1|p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/verify.txt" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$RUNNER_TEMP/files.txt"
          [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/files.txt" ] || { echo "::error::no verified files"; exit 1; }
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/out"
          (cd "$dir" && xargs sha256sum -- < "$RUNNER_TEMP/files.txt") > "$RUNNER_TEMP/out/SHA256SUMS"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/out/SHA256SUMS"
      - name: Sign and attach
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/out
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json SHA256SUMS
          gh release upload "model-guardspec-classifier-$VERSION" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber -- SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json
          {
            echo "Signed model-guardspec-classifier-$VERSION:"
            echo
            echo '```'
            cat SHA256SUMS
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Sets the guardspec_app password from GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD, like the compose
# db-roles service. Run the migrations before installing, or enable
# migrations (a hook of weight -10, so it runs first).
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: {{ include "guard-spec.fullname" . }}-db-roles
  labels:
    {{- include "guard-spec.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
  annotations:
    helm.sh/hook: pre-install,pre-upgrade
    helm.sh/hook-weight: "0"
    helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded
spec:
  backoffLimit: 3
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      {{- /* The postgres image runs as root unless told otherwise, so
      runAsNonRoot needs a UID: 70, its postgres user, unless the values set
      one. OpenShift (security.openshift.io/v1) assigns one from the
      namespace range instead, and rejects a fixed UID outside it. */}}
      {{- $psc := deepCopy (.Values.dbRoles.podSecurityContext | default dict) }}
      {{- if and (not (hasKey $psc "runAsUser")) (not (.Capabilities.APIVersions.Has "security.openshift.io/v1")) }}
      {{- $_ := set $psc "runAsUser" 70 }}

            - |

                psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -v app_password="$GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD"
              echo "guardspec_app password set"
          env:

            - {name: PGPORT, value: {{ .Values.externalDatabase.port | quote }}}
            - {name: PGDATABASE, value: {{ .Values.externalDatabase.database | quote }}}
            - {name: PGUSER, value: {{ .Values.externalDatabase.ownerUser | quote }}}
            - {name: PGSSLMODE, value: {{ .Values.externalDatabase.sslmode | quote }}}
            - name: PGPASSWORD

# ==> .github/workflows/sign-model-release.yml <==
name: Sign model release

# Manual, from main. Signs the files of a model release (tag
# model-guardspec-classifier-<version>, attached by hand, docs/models.md):
# downloads them, checks every file against the size and SHA-256 pinned for
# that version in models/manifest.yaml (go run ./cmd/models verify), writes
# SHA256SUMS for the files that matched, signs it with cosign keyless (GitHub
# OIDC, no long-lived key) and attaches SHA256SUMS and
# SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json to the release. A file that does not match its pin
# fails the run and nothing is signed. Run it again after replacing a file.
#
# This is a signature, not build provenance: the model is trained outside
# GitHub Actions, so no workflow can honestly claim to have built it. Verify:
# docs/security/verifying-releases.md.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Model version (release tag model-guardspec-classifier-<version>)
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  sign:
    # The signing identity names the ref; verification pins refs/heads/main.
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write   # attach the signature to the release
      id-token: write   # cosign keyless signing through GitHub OIDC
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - name: Download and check against models/manifest.yaml
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          case "$VERSION" in ""|*[!a-z0-9.-]*) echo "::error::bad version: $VERSION"; exit 1 ;; esac
          dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/m/guardspec-classifier/$VERSION"
          gh release download "model-guardspec-classifier-$VERSION" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -D "$dir"
          go run ./cmd/models verify -dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/m" "guardspec-classifier@$VERSION" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/verify.txt"
          # Only the files the manifest pins and that matched ("<path>: ok").
          sed -n 's|^.*/\([^/]*\): ok$|\1|p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/verify.txt" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$RUNNER_TEMP/files.txt"
          [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/files.txt" ] || { echo "::error::no verified files"; exit 1; }
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/out"
          (cd "$dir" && xargs sha256sum -- < "$RUNNER_TEMP/files.txt") > "$RUNNER_TEMP/out/SHA256SUMS"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/out/SHA256SUMS"
      - name: Sign and attach
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}/out
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json SHA256SUMS
          gh release upload "model-guardspec-classifier-$VERSION" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber -- SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json
          {
            echo "Signed model-guardspec-classifier-$VERSION:"
            echo
            echo '```'
            cat SHA256SUMS
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
label: benign

limits:
          cpus: "${GATEWAY_CPUS:-2}"
          memory: ${GATEWAY_MEMORY:-2g}
    logging: *logging

  control-plane:
    image: ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-control-plane:${GUARDSPEC_VERSION:-0.4.1}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://guardspec_app@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-guardspec}?sslmode=disable
      PGPASSWORD: ${GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD:?set GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD in .env}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?set JWT_SECRET in .env}
      MFA_ENC_KEY: ${MFA_ENC_KEY:?set MFA_ENC_KEY in .env (openssl rand -base64 32) and back it up}
      # Opens the stored content the gateway encrypted (same value as there).
      CONTENT_KEK: ${CONTENT_KEK:-}
      # Signs the activity log's hash chains every AUDIT_ANCHOR_INTERVAL (1h):
      # an Ed25519 seed, 32 random bytes in base64 (openssl rand -base64 32).
      AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY: ${AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY:-}
      ADMIN_EMAIL: ${ADMIN_EMAIL:-}
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-}
      ALLOWED_ORIGINS: https://${ADMIN_HOST}
      PUBLIC_BASE_URL: ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL:-https://${ADMIN_HOST}}
      # Caddy's address is on the edge network: believe its X-Forwarded-For,
      # so that login rate limits and audit see the real client.
      TRUSTED_PROXIES: ${EDGE_SUBNET:-172.30.89.0/24}
      UPSTREAM_LLM_URL: ${UPSTREAM_LLM_URL:-}
      UPSTREAM_KEY_ORGS: "${UPSTREAM_KEY_ORGS:-}"
      UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE: ${CONTROL_PLANE_UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE:-false}
      # Where the Models page reads the gateway's /readyz (server side, on the
      # backend network).
      GATEWAY_URL: ${GATEWAY_URL:-http://gateway:8080}
      OIDC_SECRET_GOOGLE: ${OIDC_SECRET_GOOGLE:-}
      ALERTS_SECRET_ORGS: ${ALERTS_SECRET_ORGS:-}
      ALERTS_PRIVATE_ORGS: ${ALERTS_PRIVATE_ORGS:-}
      ALERTS_EMAIL_DAILY_CAP: ${ALERTS_EMAIL_DAILY_CAP:-500}
      ALERTS_LANG: ${ALERTS_LANG:-en}
      TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: ${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME: ${TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME:-}
      TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET: ${TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET:-}
      TELEGRAM_POLLING: ${TELEGRAM_POLLING:-}
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      SMTP_URL: ${SMTP_URL:-}
      SMTP_FROM: ${SMTP_FROM:-}
      METRICS_ADDR: ":9091"
      AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS: ${AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS:-90}
      ACTIVITY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS: ${ACTIVITY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS:-365}
      SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS: ${SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS:-30}
    networks: [edge, backend]
    depends_on:
      db-roles:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    # The image's own check (its binary's "health" subcommand; the image is
    # distroless, no shell or curl), with these timings.
    healthcheck:
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "${CONTROL_PLANE_CPUS:-1}"
          memory: ${CONTROL_PLANE_MEMORY:-256m}
    logging: *logging

  postgres:
    image: postgres:17.11-alpine@sha256:266d3c257594e195b309ae9d1805e54c788f1d7b375f56bf6c367aac6c917e7b
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-guardspec}
      POSTGRES_USER: ps
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    networks: [backend]
    shm_size: 256m
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ps -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-guardspec}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "${POSTGRES_CPUS:-2}"
          memory: ${POSTGRES_MEMORY:-1g}
    logging: *logging

  # One-shot jobs, run on every `up` before the services they feed.
  migrate:
    image: migrate/migrate:v4.20.1@sha256:76cc2074cb6642631f34a898ced71e6aeaa6b1a4d78c4daa743275a22e0c5be7
    command:
      - -path=/migrations
      - -database=postgres://ps@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-guardspec}?sslmode=disable
      - up
    environment:
      PGPASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - ../../../migrations:/migrations:ro
    networks: [backend]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"
    logging: *logging

  db-roles:
    image: postgres:17.11-alpine@sha256:266d3c257594e195b309ae9d1805e54c788f1d7b375f56bf6c367aac6c917e7b
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/set-app-password.sh"]
    environment:
      PGHOST: postgres
      PGUSER: ps
      PGDATABASE: ${POSTGRES_DB:-guardspec}
      PGPASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD: ${GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD:?set GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - ../../postgres/set-app-password.sh:/set-app-password.sh:ro
    networks: [backend]
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    restart: "no"
    logging: *logging

  # Pulls the models the configured layers need into the models volume,
  # verifying SHA-256; does nothing when they are there. Same logic as the
  # quick start's models-init. Fails the stack when a pull fails, because
  # DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML defaults to true here.
  models-init:
    image: ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:${GUARDSPEC_VERSION:-0.4.1}
    # models init reads DETECTOR_LAYERS, L2_MODEL and DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML (the image has no shell).
    entrypoint: ["./models", "init", "-manifest", "manifest.yaml", "-dir", "/models/cache"]
    user: "0:0"   # writes the volume; the gateway reads it as nobody
    environment:
      MODELS_MIRROR: ${MODELS_MIRROR:-}
      DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML: ${DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML:-true}
      DETECTOR_LAYERS: ${DETECTOR_LAYERS:-l1,l2,l3}
      L2_MODEL: ${L2_MODEL:-}
    volumes:
      - models:/models
    networks: [edge]   # needs the internet (or MODELS_MIRROR)
    restart: "no"
    logging: *logging

  # Other models or versions on demand (rollback, docs/upgrade.md):
  #   docker compose --profile models run --rm models-pull guardspec-classifier@v3b
  models-pull:
    profiles: [models]
    image: ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:${GUARDSPEC_VERSION:-0.4.1}
    entrypoint: ["./models", "pull", "-manifest", "manifest.yaml", "-dir", "/models/cache"]
    user: "0:0"
    environment:
      HF_TOKEN: ${HF_TOKEN:-}
      MODELS_MIRROR: ${MODELS_MIRROR:-}
    volumes:
      - models:/models
    networks: [edge]
    restart: "no"

  # Shared scan cache for SCAN_CACHE_BACKEND=redis, on the internal network
  # only and with a required password (whoever can write to it can mark
  # content as clean). Valkey: Redis-compatible, BSD licensed. In memory only.
  #   docker compose --profile scan-cache up -d
  #   SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_URL=redis://:<SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD>@scan-cache:6379/0
  scan-cache:
    profiles: [scan-cache]
    image: valkey/valkey:8.1.4-alpine@sha256:e706d1213aaba6896c162bb6a3a9e1894e1a435f28f8f856d14fab2e10aa098b
    restart: unless-stopped
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        if [ "$${#SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD}" -lt 16 ]; then
          echo "scan-cache: set SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD (16 characters or more) in .env" >&2; exit 1
        fi
        exec valkey-server --requirepass "$$SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD" --save "" --appendonly no \
          --maxmemory "$${SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_MAXMEMORY:-256mb}" --maxmemory-policy volatile-lru
    environment:
      SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD: ${SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD:-}
      SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_MAXMEMORY: ${SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_MAXMEMORY:-256mb}
    networks: [backend]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "valkey-cli --no-auth-warning -a \"$$SCAN_CACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD\" ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.5"
          memory: ${SCAN_CACHE_MEMORY:-320m}
    logging: *logging

networks:
  # Caddy, the services and egress (upstream LLMs, SMTP, model downloads).
  # The fixed subnet is what the control plane's TRUSTED_PROXIES trusts;
  # change EDGE_SUBNET if it collides with one of your networks.
  edge:
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${EDGE_SUBNET:-172.30.89.0/24}
  # Postgres and the jobs: no route to the outside.
  backend:

{{- $name := printf "%s-control-plane" (include "guard-spec.fullname" .) -}}

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:

  labels:
    {{- include "guard-spec.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: control-plane
spec:
  {{- if not .Values.controlPlane.autoscaling.enabled }}
  replicas: {{ .Values.controlPlane.replicaCount }}
  {{- end }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "guard-spec.selector" $sel | nindent 6 }}
  template:
    metadata:
      {{- include "guard-spec.podMetadata" $sel | nindent 6 }}
    spec:
      {{- with include "guard-spec.serviceAccountName" . }}
      serviceAccountName: {{ . }}
      {{- end }}
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      {{- with .Values.imagePullSecrets }}
      imagePullSecrets:
        {{- toYaml . | nindent 8 }}
      {{- end }}
      securityContext:
        {{- toYaml .Values.podSecurityContext | nindent 8 }}
      containers:
        - name: control-plane
          image: {{ include "guard-spec.image" (dict "root" . "image" .Values.controlPlane.image) }}
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.controlPlane.image.pullPolicy }}
          securityContext:
            {{- toYaml .Values.securityContext | nindent 12 }}
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8081
            - name: metrics
              containerPort: {{ .Values.controlPlane.metricsPort }}
          env:
            {{- include "guard-spec.commonEnv" . | nindent 12 }}
            - name: LISTEN_ADDR
              value: ":8081"
            - name: METRICS_ADDR
              value: {{ printf ":%v" .Values.controlPlane.metricsPort | quote }}
            - name: JWT_SECRET
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ .Values.existingSecret }}
                  key: JWT_SECRET
            # Optional: without MFA_ENC_KEY in the Secret the variable is not
            # set here, and it can still come from controlPlane.extraEnvFrom.
            - name: MFA_ENC_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ .Values.existingSecret }}
                  key: MFA_ENC_KEY
                  optional: true
            # Optional: without CONTENT_KEK in the Secret the variable is not
            # set; stored content is then kept in the clear (docs/security).
            - name: CONTENT_KEK
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ .Values.existingSecret }}
                  key: CONTENT_KEK
                  optional: true
            - name: AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ .Values.existingSecret }}
                  key: AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY
                  optional: true
            {{- if .Values.controlPlane.adminEmail }}
            - name: ADMIN_EMAIL
              value: {{ .Values.controlPlane.adminEmail | quote }}
            - name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ .Values.existingSecret }}
                  key: ADMIN_PASSWORD
            {{- end }}
            {{- $gw := include "guard-spec.gatewayURL" . }}
            {{- if $gw }}
            - name: GATEWAY_URL
              value: {{ $gw | quote }}
            {{- end }}
            {{- if .Values.gateway.adminListener.enabled }}
            {{- if not .Values.controlPlane.gatewayTLSSecret }}
            {{- fail "gateway.adminListener.enabled needs controlPlane.gatewayTLSSecret (the control plane's client certificate: tls.crt, tls.key, ca.crt)" }}
            {{- end }}
            - name: GATEWAY_TLS_CERT_FILE
              value: /run/guard-spec/gateway-tls/tls.crt
            - name: GATEWAY_TLS_KEY_FILE

    steps:

text:
#
# A vulnerability that does not apply to Guard Spec is recorded, with the
# reason, in .vex/guard-spec.openvex.json, which every scan reads.
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "41 2 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: vuln-scan-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Trivy and the gateway's ONNX archives are kept in the Actions cache (keyed
# by the scripts that pin their versions and SHA-256 values), so a GitHub
# Releases outage does not fail the scans. A cached file gets the same
# SHA-256 check as a downloaded one.

env:
  # The Trivy DB, with a fallback when ghcr.io rate-limits.
  TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY: mirror.gcr.io/aquasec/trivy-db,ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-db
  TRIVY_JAVA_DB_REPOSITORY: mirror.gcr.io/aquasec/trivy-java-db,ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-java-db
  TRIVY_VEX: .vex/guard-spec.openvex.json
  TRIVY_SCANNERS: vuln
  TRIVY_NO_PROGRESS: "true"

jobs:
  dependencies:
    name: Dependencies (lockfiles)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write   # SARIF to Code scanning
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        id: trivy-cache
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
          key: trivy-linux-amd64-${{ hashFiles('scripts/install-trivy.sh') }}
      - run: scripts/install-trivy.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" && echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        env:
          DOWNLOAD_CACHE: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
      - uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: steps.trivy-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
          key: ${{ steps.trivy-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - name: Report every finding
        run: trivy fs --format sarif --output deps.sarif .
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@1fc58d04a4d4374f921bdac573c3811c240f9c26 # v4
        if: always() && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
        with:
          sarif_file: deps.sarif
          category: trivy-dependencies
      - name: Fail on a vulnerability that has a fix
        run: trivy fs --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 .

  images:
    name: Images (built from this checkout)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        image: [gateway, control-plane]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        id: trivy-cache
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
          key: trivy-linux-amd64-${{ hashFiles('scripts/install-trivy.sh') }}
      - run: scripts/install-trivy.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" && echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        env:
          DOWNLOAD_CACHE: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
      - uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: steps.trivy-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
          key: ${{ steps.trivy-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        id: onnx-cache
        if: matrix.image == 'gateway'
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/onnx-deps
          key: onnx-deps-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('build/onnx-deps.sh') }}
      # The gateway build takes the ONNX archives from the cache through a
      # build context; this step fills it, or checks the restored archives.
      - name: ONNX archives for the gateway image
        if: matrix.image == 'gateway'
        run: sh build/onnx-deps.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/onnx"
        env:
          ONNX_DEPS_CACHE: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/onnx-deps
      - uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: matrix.image == 'gateway' && steps.onnx-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/onnx-deps
          key: ${{ steps.onnx-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - name: Build
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
          ONNX_DEPS_CACHE: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/onnx-deps
        run: |
          set --
          if [ "$IMAGE" = gateway ]; then
            set -- --build-context "onnx-cache=$ONNX_DEPS_CACHE" --build-arg ONNX_DEPS_CACHE=/onnx-cache
          fi
          docker build "$@" -f "build/$IMAGE.Dockerfile" -t "guard-spec-$IMAGE:scan" .
      - name: Report every finding
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
        run: trivy image --format sarif --output image.sarif "guard-spec-$IMAGE:scan"
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@1fc58d04a4d4374f921bdac573c3811c240f9c26 # v4
        if: always() && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)
        with:
          sarif_file: image.sarif
          category: trivy-image-${{ matrix.image }}
      - name: Fail on a vulnerability that has a fix
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
        run: trivy image --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 "guard-spec-$IMAGE:scan"

  released:
    name: Images of the latest release
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write   # one "security" issue per release with findings
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        id: trivy-cache
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
          key: trivy-linux-amd64-${{ hashFiles('scripts/install-trivy.sh') }}
      - run: scripts/install-trivy.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" && echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        env:
          DOWNLOAD_CACHE: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
      - uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: steps.trivy-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/dl/trivy
          key: ${{ steps.trivy-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - name: Scan
        id: scan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
        run: |
          tag=$(gh release list --exclude-pre-releases --exclude-drafts --limit 50 --json tagName,isLatest \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.tagName | startswith("v"))] | (map(select(.isLatest)) + .)[0].tagName')
          version=${tag#v}
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          reports=""
          for image in gateway gateway-full control-plane; do
            ref="ghcr.io/$OWNER/guard-spec-$image:$version"
            if ! docker manifest inspect "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "$ref: not published, skipped"
              continue
            fi
            trivy image --format json --output "$image.json" "$ref"
            reports="$reports $image.json"
          done
          set +e
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # one argument per report
          python3 scripts/vuln-report.py "Known vulnerabilities in the v$version images" $reports > body.md
          echo "found=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          cat body.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Open, update or close the issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.version }}
          FOUND: ${{ steps.scan.outputs.found }}
        run: |
          export TITLE="Known vulnerabilities in the v$VERSION images"

RUN set -eu; \
    ./models pull -manifest manifest.yaml -models multilingual-e5-small -dir /tmp/pull; \
    src=$(dirname "$(find /tmp/pull -name model.onnx -path '*multilingual-e5-small*' | head -n 1)"); \
    test -f "$src/tokenizer.json" && test -f "$src/config.json"; \
    mkdir -p /models/cache; \
    mv "$src" /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small; \
    rm -rf /tmp/pull; \
    find /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small -name '.*' -exec rm -rf {} +; \
    chown -R root:root /models; \
    chmod -R a=rX /models; \
    ls -lR /models

    L2_MODEL_DIR=/models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b \
    L3_MODEL_DIR=/models/cache/multilingual-e5-small \
    DETECTOR_LAYERS=l1,l2,l3 \

# air-gapped installs (no `models pull`, no /models mount). It adds:
#
#   L2  guardspec-classifier-v3b  /models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b/
#       model_int8.onnx, tokenizer.json, config.json, thresholds.json,
#       calibration.json; checked against build/gateway-full.l2.sha256.
#   L3  multilingual-e5-small     /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small/
#       pulled by the image's own `models` tool from its manifest.yaml, which
#       pins a Hugging Face commit and the SHA-256 of every file.
#
# Build (the L2 files come from a named build context, a directory holding
# them; CI fills it with `go run ./cmd/models pull`, see release.yml):
#
#   docker buildx build -f build/gateway-full.Dockerfile \
#     --build-arg GATEWAY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:<version> \
#     --build-context l2=<dir with the five L2 files> \
#     -t guard-spec-gateway-full:<version> .
#
# The models are owned by root and read-only; the gateway runs as the same
# non-root user as the gateway image (nobody). Only the L3 pull needs network,
# at build time; the image itself needs none.

# The gateway image to extend: a released tag or digest, or a local build of
# build/gateway.Dockerfile (docker-compose.yml tags it guard-spec-gateway:latest;
# pass --build-arg GATEWAY_IMAGE=guard-spec-gateway:latest to use it). The
# default is the signed v0.4.0 release, pinned by the digest of its index, so a
# build without the argument never pulls a moving tag. The release workflow
# always passes the digest of the gateway image it has just built and signed.
ARG GATEWAY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:0.4.0@sha256:e69b343e392d2eadc2f8a4850c2044aa8b917b0e853b45d284fce7e5978af077

# --build-context l2=... stops below with a clear message.
FROM scratch AS l2

FROM ${GATEWAY_IMAGE} AS gateway

# The gateway image has no shell (distroless), so the models are assembled in
# a Debian stage that is not shipped: it runs the image's own models tool and
# manifest, with the image's CA certificates.
FROM debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:734a72b3d6142a71993b4bc580ca01d8ca687f77a2c422d96a961d3376b179bc AS models

COPY --from=gateway /app/models /app/manifest.yaml ./
COPY --from=gateway /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
COPY build/gateway-full.l2.sha256 /tmp/l2.sha256
COPY --from=l2 / /tmp/l2/
# L2: exactly the files listed in build/gateway-full.l2.sha256, each verified.
RUN set -eu; \
    dest=/models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b; \
    if [ ! -s /tmp/l2/model_int8.onnx ]; then \
      echo "gateway-full: no L2 model. Pass --build-context l2=<dir> with the files of build/gateway-full.l2.sha256." >&2; \
      exit 1; \
    fi; \
    (cd /tmp/l2 && sha256sum --strict -c /tmp/l2.sha256); \
    mkdir -p "$dest"; \
    awk '{print $2}' /tmp/l2.sha256 | while read -r f; do cp "/tmp/l2/$f" "$dest/$f"; done; \
    rm -rf /tmp/l2 /tmp/l2.sha256
# L3: the image's own models tool and manifest (SHA-256 verified). It pulls into
# a scratch directory and the model directory is moved into place, so the
# result does not depend on the tool's cache layout.
RUN set -eu; \
    ./models pull -manifest manifest.yaml -models multilingual-e5-small -dir /tmp/pull; \
    src=$(dirname "$(find /tmp/pull -name model.onnx -path '*multilingual-e5-small*' | head -n 1)"); \
    test -f "$src/tokenizer.json" && test -f "$src/config.json"; \
    mkdir -p /models/cache; \
    mv "$src" /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small; \
    rm -rf /tmp/pull; \
    find /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small -name '.*' -exec rm -rf {} +; \
    chown -R root:root /models; \
    chmod -R a=rX /models; \
    ls -lR /models

FROM ${GATEWAY_IMAGE}
COPY --from=models /models /models
# Explicit model directories: they work whether the gateway resolves L2 from
# L2_MODEL_DIR or from L2_MODEL=name@version. DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML=true: the
# models are in the image, so a layer that fails to load is an error, not a
# silent fall back to L1 (GUARD_ENV=dev turns that into a warning).
ENV MODEL_DIR=/models \
    L2_MODEL_DIR=/models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b \
    L3_MODEL_DIR=/models/cache/multilingual-e5-small \
    DETECTOR_LAYERS=l1,l2,l3 \
    DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML=true
USER nobody

# ==> build/gateway.Dockerfile <==
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Gateway: Go data plane with in-process ONNX Runtime (internal/onnx).
#
# Builds for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (docker buildx --platform ...).
# The `onnx` build tag needs cgo: libtokenizers.a is linked statically and
# libonnxruntime.so is shipped in the image and loaded at run time
# (ONNXRUNTIME_LIB). Versions and SHA-256 values live in build/onnx-deps.sh.

# Default for the `onnx-cache` build context: empty. CI passes
#   --build-context onnx-cache=<dir> --build-arg ONNX_DEPS_CACHE=/onnx-cache
# with the archives from actions/cache, so a GitHub Releases outage does not
# fail the build; onnx-deps.sh still checks every SHA-256. Releases and local
# builds pass neither and download as before.
FROM scratch AS onnx-cache

FROM golang:1.26.10-bookworm@sha256:23ce71337b726608afb1bc00986e630a05034a87a87ea1fc2cd1ae5cf33387eb AS builder
ARG TARGETOS=linux
ARG TARGETARCH
# Release version, linked into the binaries (gateway --version).
ARG VERSION=dev

WORKDIR /src
COPY build/onnx-deps.sh /tmp/onnx-deps.sh
ARG ONNX_DEPS_CACHE
RUN --mount=type=bind,from=onnx-cache,target=/onnx-cache \
    sh /tmp/onnx-deps.sh /opt/onnx "$TARGETOS" "${TARGETARCH:-$(uname -m)}"

COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download

COPY . .
ENV CGO_ENABLED=1 CGO_LDFLAGS=-L/opt/onnx/lib GOTOOLCHAIN=local
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    go build -tags onnx -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X github.com/guard-spec/guard-spec/internal/version.Version=${VERSION#v}" -o /out/gateway ./cmd/gateway/ \
 && go build -tags onnx -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/onnxbench ./cmd/onnxbench/ \
 && go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X github.com/guard-spec/guard-spec/internal/version.Version=${VERSION#v}" -o /out/models ./cmd/models/ \
 && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X github.com/guard-spec/guard-spec/internal/version.Version=${VERSION#v}" -o /out/doctor ./cmd/doctor/

# --- dist: the linux onnx tarball of a release (.github/workflows/release.yml) ---
# docker buildx build --target dist --output type=local,dest=out ...
# Same binary as the image; it needs glibc >= 2.36 (Debian 12) at run time and
# ONNXRUNTIME_LIB pointing at the bundled libonnxruntime.so.
FROM scratch AS dist
COPY --from=builder /out/gateway /out/models /out/doctor /
COPY --from=builder /opt/onnx/lib/libonnxruntime.so /lib/
COPY --from=builder /opt/onnx/LICENSE.onnxruntime /src/LICENSE /src/NOTICE /src/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md /src/models/manifest.yaml /

# --- runtime image (default target) ---
# Chainguard glibc-dynamic (Wolfi): glibc, libgcc, libstdc++ and CA
# certificates only, rebuilt daily with fixes; no shell, package manager or
# curl. Debian bookworm-slim carried hundreds of OS CVEs without a fix; this
# base has none at the pinned digest (Dependabot bumps it). The binaries are
# built on Debian 12 (glibc 2.36) and run on the newer glibc of Wolfi. The
# HEALTHCHECK, compose and Kubernetes use the binaries' own subcommands
# (gateway health, models init, doctor copy-migrations) instead of scripts.
FROM cgr.dev/chainguard/glibc-dynamic:latest@sha256:aab5cd0b4cc5edd9c87b6e7aa9ddaa3fb6ffcec559b9e5473c55bbc937b65399

# ONNX Runtime CPU shared library (MIT), loaded by internal/onnx via dlopen.
COPY --from=builder /opt/onnx/lib/libonnxruntime.so /usr/local/lib/
COPY --from=builder /opt/onnx/LICENSE.onnxruntime /usr/share/doc/onnxruntime/LICENSE
# Model files are mounted at /models (read-only is fine), never baked in. An
# empty /models: the gateway warns and runs L1 only; /readyz shows the layers.
ENV ONNXRUNTIME_LIB=/usr/local/lib/libonnxruntime.so \
    MODEL_DIR=/models

WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /out/gateway /out/onnxbench /out/models /out/doctor ./
COPY --from=builder /src/migrations ./migrations

# Copyright 2026 The Guard Spec Authors
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#
# gateway-full: the released gateway image with its models baked in, for
# air-gapped installs (no `models pull`, no /models mount). It adds:
#
#   L2  guardspec-classifier-v3b  /models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b/
#       model_int8.onnx, tokenizer.json, config.json, thresholds.json,
#       calibration.json; checked against build/gateway-full.l2.sha256.
#   L3  multilingual-e5-small     /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small/
#       pulled by the image's own `models` tool from its manifest.yaml, which
#       pins a Hugging Face commit and the SHA-256 of every file.
#
# Build (the L2 files come from a named build context, a directory holding
# them; CI fills it with `go run ./cmd/models pull`, see release.yml):
#
#   docker buildx build -f build/gateway-full.Dockerfile \
#     --build-arg GATEWAY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:<version> \
#     --build-context l2=<dir with the five L2 files> \
#     -t guard-spec-gateway-full:<version> .
#
# The models are owned by root and read-only; the gateway runs as the same
# non-root user as the gateway image (nobody). Only the L3 pull needs network,
# at build time; the image itself needs none.

# The gateway image to extend: a released tag or digest, or a local build of
# build/gateway.Dockerfile (docker-compose.yml tags it guard-spec-gateway:latest;
# pass --build-arg GATEWAY_IMAGE=guard-spec-gateway:latest to use it). The
# default is the signed v0.4.0 release, pinned by the digest of its index, so a
# build without the argument never pulls a moving tag. The release workflow
# always passes the digest of the gateway image it has just built and signed.
ARG GATEWAY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/guard-spec/guard-spec-gateway:0.4.0@sha256:e69b343e392d2eadc2f8a4850c2044aa8b917b0e853b45d284fce7e5978af077

# Default for the `l2` build context: empty, so a build without
# --build-context l2=... stops below with a clear message.
FROM scratch AS l2

FROM ${GATEWAY_IMAGE} AS gateway

# The gateway image has no shell (distroless), so the models are assembled in
# a Debian stage that is not shipped: it runs the image's own models tool and
# manifest, with the image's CA certificates.
FROM debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:734a72b3d6142a71993b4bc580ca01d8ca687f77a2c422d96a961d3376b179bc AS models
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=gateway /app/models /app/manifest.yaml ./
COPY --from=gateway /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
COPY build/gateway-full.l2.sha256 /tmp/l2.sha256
COPY --from=l2 / /tmp/l2/
# L2: exactly the files listed in build/gateway-full.l2.sha256, each verified.
RUN set -eu; \
    dest=/models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b; \
    if [ ! -s /tmp/l2/model_int8.onnx ]; then \
      echo "gateway-full: no L2 model. Pass --build-context l2=<dir> with the files of build/gateway-full.l2.sha256." >&2; \
      exit 1; \
    fi; \
    (cd /tmp/l2 && sha256sum --strict -c /tmp/l2.sha256); \
    mkdir -p "$dest"; \
    awk '{print $2}' /tmp/l2.sha256 | while read -r f; do cp "/tmp/l2/$f" "$dest/$f"; done; \
    rm -rf /tmp/l2 /tmp/l2.sha256
# L3: the image's own models tool and manifest (SHA-256 verified). It pulls into
# a scratch directory and the model directory is moved into place, so the
# result does not depend on the tool's cache layout.
RUN set -eu; \
    ./models pull -manifest manifest.yaml -models multilingual-e5-small -dir /tmp/pull; \
    src=$(dirname "$(find /tmp/pull -name model.onnx -path '*multilingual-e5-small*' | head -n 1)"); \
    test -f "$src/tokenizer.json" && test -f "$src/config.json"; \
    mkdir -p /models/cache; \
    mv "$src" /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small; \
    rm -rf /tmp/pull; \
    find /models/cache/multilingual-e5-small -name '.*' -exec rm -rf {} +; \
    chown -R root:root /models; \
    chmod -R a=rX /models; \
    ls -lR /models

FROM ${GATEWAY_IMAGE}
COPY --from=models /models /models
# Explicit model directories: they work whether the gateway resolves L2 from
# L2_MODEL_DIR or from L2_MODEL=name@version. DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML=true: the
# models are in the image, so a layer that fails to load is an error, not a
# silent fall back to L1 (GUARD_ENV=dev turns that into a warning).
ENV MODEL_DIR=/models \
    L2_MODEL_DIR=/models/local/guardspec-classifier-v3b \
    L3_MODEL_DIR=/models/cache/multilingual-e5-small \
    DETECTOR_LAYERS=l1,l2,l3 \
    DETECTOR_REQUIRE_ML=true
USER nobody

    USING (org_id = current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON invites TO guardspec_app;

-- The org is unknown until the token is resolved, so claiming runs with the
-- owner's rights, like lookup_api_key. It marks one pending, unexpired invite
-- accepted and returns it; called inside the accepting transaction, a failure
-- later in that transaction rolls the claim back.
CREATE FUNCTION claim_invite(hash TEXT)
RETURNS TABLE (invite_id UUID, org_id UUID, email TEXT, role org_role)
LANGUAGE sql VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp
AS $$
    UPDATE invites i SET accepted_at = NOW()
    WHERE i.token_hash = hash
      AND i.accepted_at IS NULL
      AND i.revoked_at IS NULL
      AND i.expires_at > NOW()
    RETURNING i.id, i.org_id, i.email, i.role
$$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION claim_invite(TEXT) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION claim_invite(TEXT) TO guardspec_app;

-- Audit retention. Rows of every org are deleted, which RLS does not let guardspec_app
-- do, so the batch delete runs with the owner's rights. It removes at most
-- batch rows older than cutoff and returns how many it removed.
CREATE INDEX idx_requests_created ON requests (created_at);

CREATE FUNCTION purge_audit_rows(cutoff TIMESTAMPTZ, batch INT)
RETURNS INT
LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp
AS $$
DECLARE
    n INT;
BEGIN
    IF batch IS NULL OR batch < 1 OR batch > 100000 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'batch must be between 1 and 100000';
    END IF;
    DELETE FROM requests WHERE id IN (
        SELECT id FROM requests WHERE created_at < cutoff
        ORDER BY created_at LIMIT batch
        FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
    );
    GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
    RETURN n;
END
$$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION purge_audit_rows(TIMESTAMPTZ, INT) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION purge_audit_rows(TIMESTAMPTZ, INT) TO guardspec_app;

-- SIEM export (RF-f2f95010). Each sink sends an organization's events
-- (events table: detections, security, configuration and activity events;
-- metadata only) as OCSF records to Splunk HEC, Elasticsearch, Microsoft
-- Sentinel, syslog over TLS or an HTTP endpoint. The cursor is the last
-- event delivered, by (created_at, id); delivery is at least once.
CREATE TABLE siem_sinks (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    org_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name            TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT siem_sinks_name CHECK (char_length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
    kind            TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT siem_sinks_kind CHECK (kind IN ('splunk_hec', 'elastic', 'sentinel', 'syslog', 'http')),
    -- Non-secret settings: URLs, index, tenant and client ids, CA PEM.
    config          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' CONSTRAINT siem_sinks_config CHECK (pg_column_size(config) <= 16384),
    -- The variable holding the secret (ALERTS_SECRET_ORGS kind siem), never the secret.
    secret_env      TEXT CONSTRAINT siem_sinks_secret_env CHECK (secret_env ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,63}$'),
    -- Event types to send (exact, or a family such as "detection."); NULL: all.
    event_types     TEXT[],
    min_severity    alert_severity NOT NULL DEFAULT 'info',
    allow_private   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    enabled         BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    cursor_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    cursor_id       UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000',
    next_attempt_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    failures        INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_error      TEXT CONSTRAINT siem_sinks_last_error CHECK (char_length(last_error) <= 1000),
    last_success_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    delivered       BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_siem_sinks_org ON siem_sinks (org_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_siem_sinks_due ON siem_sinks (next_attempt_at) WHERE enabled;
CREATE INDEX idx_events_org_created ON events (org_id, created_at, id);
ALTER TABLE siem_sinks ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_siem_sinks ON siem_sinks
    USING (org_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.org_id', true), '')::uuid);
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON siem_sinks TO guardspec_app;

-- The export worker claims due sinks of every organization (RLS hides them
-- from guardspec_app otherwise) for lease: another control plane replica
-- skips a claimed sink until the lease ends or the worker reschedules it.
CREATE FUNCTION claim_siem_sinks(lease INTERVAL, max_sinks INT)
RETURNS TABLE (org_id UUID, id UUID)
LANGUAGE sql VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp
AS $$
    UPDATE siem_sinks s SET next_attempt_at = NOW() + lease
    WHERE s.id IN (
        SELECT x.id FROM siem_sinks x WHERE x.enabled AND x.next_attempt_at <= NOW()
        ORDER BY x.next_attempt_at LIMIT max_sinks FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
    RETURNING s.org_id, s.id
$$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION claim_siem_sinks(INTERVAL, INT) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION claim_siem_sinks(INTERVAL, INT) TO guardspec_app;

-- One instance administrator: the earliest owner of the default organization
-- (seeded by 002), which is the bootstrap admin (ADMIN_EMAIL) on an instance
-- set up by the control plane. Other owners are not promoted. The control
-- plane promotes ADMIN_EMAIL at startup if no instance administrator exists.

WHERE id = (SELECT user_id FROM org_memberships
            WHERE org_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001' AND role = 'owner'
            ORDER BY joined_at, user_id LIMIT 1);

-- One row per login. The JWT carries the id as "sid"; a revoked or expired
-- row ends the session before the token does.
CREATE TABLE sessions (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    -- password, google or oidc:<provider id>
    method       TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT sessions_method CHECK (char_length(method) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
    -- true when a TOTP or recovery code was checked at login
    mfa          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    user_agent   TEXT CONSTRAINT sessions_user_agent CHECK (char_length(user_agent) <= 512),
    ip           TEXT CONSTRAINT sessions_ip CHECK (char_length(ip) <= 64),
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked_at   TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_user ON sessions (user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_expires ON sessions (expires_at);

-- Instance-wide SSO providers. The client secret is read from the variable
-- client_secret_env names, never stored.
CREATE TABLE identity_providers (
    id                UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    type              TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT identity_providers_type CHECK (type IN ('google', 'oidc')),
    display_name      TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT identity_providers_display_name CHECK (char_length(display_name) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
    issuer            TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT identity_providers_issuer CHECK (char_length(issuer) BETWEEN 1 AND 2048),
    client_id         TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT identity_providers_client_id CHECK (char_length(client_id) BETWEEN 1 AND 512),
    client_secret_env TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT identity_providers_secret_env CHECK (client_secret_env ~ '^OIDC_SECRET_[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$'),
    scopes            TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{openid,email,profile}',
    allowed_domains   TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    auto_provision    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    enabled           BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- A user's SSO identities: (provider, subject) names one account.
CREATE TABLE user_identities (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES identity_providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    subject     TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT user_identities_subject CHECK (char_length(subject) BETWEEN 1 AND 255),
    email       TEXT,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    CONSTRAINT user_identities_provider_subject UNIQUE (provider_id, subject),
    CONSTRAINT user_identities_user_provider UNIQUE (user_id, provider_id)
);

-- An SSO login in progress: the state (as its SHA-256), the nonce and the
-- PKCE verifier, for 10 minutes. link_user_id is set when a logged-in user
-- links the identity from their profile.
CREATE TABLE oidc_states (
    state_hash    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    provider_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES identity_providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    nonce         TEXT NOT NULL,
    code_verifier TEXT NOT NULL,
    redirect      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '/ui/',
    link_user_id  UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    expires_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_oidc_states_expires ON oidc_states (expires_at);

-- The one-time code the callback hands the UI (60 s), exchanged for the same
-- answer as a password login. Tokens never travel in URLs.
CREATE TABLE oidc_codes (
    code_hash  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    method     TEXT NOT NULL,
    redirect   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '/ui/',
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    used_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
);
CREATE INDEX idx_oidc_codes_expires ON oidc_codes (expires_at);

-- TOTP (RFC 6238). Secrets are AES-GCM ciphertexts (MFA_ENC_KEY, the user id
-- as additional data). pending_secret_enc is a setup not yet confirmed;
-- last_used_step refuses a code a second time within its window.
CREATE TABLE user_mfa (
    user_id            UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    totp_secret_enc    BYTEA,
    pending_secret_enc BYTEA,
    enabled_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_used_step     BIGINT,
    updated_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE mfa_recovery_codes (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    code_hash  TEXT NOT NULL,
    used_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_mfa_recovery_codes_user ON mfa_recovery_codes (user_id);

-- The second step of a login (the mfa_token, a 5-minute JWT whose jti is the
-- id): purpose verify asks for a code, enroll for a 2FA setup. Each allows 5
-- attempts and one success.
CREATE TABLE mfa_challenges (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    purpose    TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT mfa_challenges_purpose CHECK (purpose IN ('verify', 'enroll')),
    method     TEXT NOT NULL,
    attempts   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    used_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_mfa_challenges_expires ON mfa_challenges (expires_at);

-- Per-organization login rules. No row: the defaults (no 2FA requirement,
-- every login method, 12-hour sessions). allowed_login_methods NULL allows all.
CREATE TABLE org_security (
    org_id                 UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    require_mfa            BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    sso_satisfies_mfa      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    allowed_login_methods  TEXT[],
    domain_join            JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    session_lifetime_hours INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 12
        CONSTRAINT org_security_session_lifetime CHECK (session_lifetime_hours BETWEEN 1 AND 12),
    updated_at             TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
ALTER TABLE org_security ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_org_security ON org_security
    USING (org_id = current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid);

-- Admin actions. org_id NULL is an instance-level row (SSO providers, instance
-- users, logins), visible only in a transaction that sets app.instance_scope,
-- which the control plane does for instance administrators.
CREATE TABLE activity_log (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    org_id      UUID REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    actor_id    UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    actor_email TEXT,
    action      TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT activity_log_action CHECK (char_length(action) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
    target      TEXT CONSTRAINT activity_log_target CHECK (char_length(target) <= 512),
    ip          TEXT CONSTRAINT activity_log_ip CHECK (char_length(ip) <= 64),
    details     JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);
CREATE INDEX idx_activity_log_org ON activity_log (org_id, at DESC, id DESC);
ALTER TABLE activity_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_activity ON activity_log
    USING (org_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.org_id', true), '')::uuid);
CREATE POLICY instance_activity ON activity_log

-- ==> migrations/019_audit_repeat_count.up.sql <==
-- Copyright 2026 The Guard Spec Authors
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

-- Retried refusals (RF-ec4c8602): a client that gets a refusal may send the
-- same request again (Claude Code sends it six times). The gateway writes the
-- first refusal's row and counts identical refusals of the same API key that
-- follow within AUDIT_DEDUPE_WINDOW (default 10 s) here, instead of writing a
-- row for each. NULL: the row stands for one request; otherwise the number of
-- requests it stands for, the first included. Allowed requests are never
-- folded. The row's other columns are the first refusal's.
--
-- The column is on requests, so the table's row level security covers it.

# for the next run. A cache entry can save a download, never skip the check.
set -eu

usage='usage: fetch-verified.sh <url> <sha256> <out>'
url=${1:?$usage}
want=${2:?$usage}
out=${3:?$usage}

sha256() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
  else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

  cached=$DOWNLOAD_CACHE/$want-${url##*/}

    if [ "$(sha256 "$out")" = "$want" ]; then
      echo "fetch-verified: ${url##*/} from the cache, sha256 ok"
      exit 0

    echo "fetch-verified: ignoring $cached: sha256 mismatch" >&2
    rm -f "$out" "$cached"

# minutes, on any error, before failing (the cache covers longer outages).

got=$(sha256 "$out")
if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
  echo "fetch-verified: sha256 mismatch for $url: got $got, want $want" >&2
  rm -f "$out"
  exit 1
fi
echo "fetch-verified: ${url##*/} downloaded, sha256 ok"
if [ -n "$cached" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$DOWNLOAD_CACHE"

# Steps: verify the dump's sha256 against MANIFEST; start postgres; refuse a
# non-empty database; create the cluster-wide role guardspec_app (pg_dump
# does not carry roles); pg_restore; restore Caddy's /data when the backup and
# the stack have it; then `docker compose up -d --wait`, whose migrate and
# db-roles jobs apply newer migrations, if any, and set the guardspec_app
# password from the env file.
#
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # $POSTGRES_DB and $1 in single quotes expand in the container
set -eu

root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
file=$root/docker-compose.yml
project=
envfile=

die() {
	echo "restore: $*" >&2
	exit 1
}

while getopts f:p:e:h opt; do
	case $opt in
	f) file=$OPTARG ;;
	p) project=$OPTARG ;;
	e) envfile=$OPTARG ;;
	*)
		sed -n '4,/^set -eu/p' "$0" | grep -v '^# shellcheck\|^set -eu' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
		exit 2
		;;
	esac
done
shift $((OPTIND - 1))
[ $# -eq 1 ] || die "usage: scripts/restore.sh [-f file] [-p project] [-e env file] BACKUP_DIR"
dir=$1

command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker is not installed"
[ -f "$file" ] || die "compose file not found: $file"
[ -f "$dir/guardspec.dump" ] || die "$dir/guardspec.dump not found"
[ -f "$dir/guardspec.env" ] || die "$dir/guardspec.env not found"
[ -n "$envfile" ] || envfile=$(dirname "$file")/.env

sha() {
	if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1"; else shasum -a 256 "$1"; fi | cut -d' ' -f1
}
if [ -f "$dir/MANIFEST" ]; then
	want=$(sed -n 's/^sha256: *\([0-9a-f]*\)  guardspec.dump$/\1/p' "$dir/MANIFEST")
	[ -z "$want" ] || [ "$want" = "$(sha "$dir/guardspec.dump")" ] ||
		die "guardspec.dump does not match the sha256 in MANIFEST"
fi

# env_get KEY FILE: the last KEY= value in FILE.
env_get() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$2" | tail -n 1; }

if [ -f "$envfile" ]; then
	if [ "$(env_get MFA_ENC_KEY "$envfile")" != "$(env_get MFA_ENC_KEY "$dir/guardspec.env")" ] &&
		[ "${RESTORE_ALLOW_KEY_CHANGE:-}" != 1 ]; then
		die "MFA_ENC_KEY in $envfile differs from the backup's: 2FA secrets in the database would not decrypt. Use the backup's guardspec.env, or set RESTORE_ALLOW_KEY_CHANGE=1"
	fi
	echo "restore: using the existing $envfile"
else
	(umask 077 && cp "$dir/guardspec.env" "$envfile")
	echo "restore: wrote $envfile from the backup (mode 600)"
fi

dc() {
	if [ -n "$project" ]; then
		docker compose -f "$file" -p "$project" --env-file "$envfile" "$@"
	else
		docker compose -f "$file" --env-file "$envfile" "$@"
	fi
}

# psql_ps SQL: runs SQL as the superuser inside the postgres container.
psql_ps() {
	dc exec -T postgres sh -c 'psql -U ps -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -tAq -c "$1"' sh "$1"
}

echo "restore: starting postgres"
dc up -d --wait postgres

n=$(psql_ps "SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public'")
[ "$n" -eq 0 ] ||
	die "the database already has $n tables; restore into an empty one (a new project, or docker compose down -v first)"

psql_ps "DO \$\$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'guardspec_app') THEN
    CREATE ROLE guardspec_app LOGIN;
  END IF;
END \$\$"

echo "restore: pg_restore $dir/guardspec.dump"
dc exec -T postgres sh -c 'pg_restore -U ps -d "$POSTGRES_DB" --exit-on-error' <"$dir/guardspec.dump" ||
	die "pg_restore failed"

if [ -f "$dir/caddy-data.tgz" ] && dc config --services | grep -qx caddy; then
	echo "restore: restoring Caddy's certificates and CA"
	dc run --rm --no-deps -T --entrypoint tar caddy -C /data -xzf - <"$dir/caddy-data.tgz"
fi

echo "restore: starting the stack"
dc up -d --wait --wait-timeout "${RESTORE_TIMEOUT:-600}"
echo "restore: done; restored rows:"
for t in organizations users api_keys policies upstreams requests; do
	printf '  %s: %s\n' "$t" "$(psql_ps "SELECT count(*) FROM $t")"
done

#!/bin/sh
# Copyright 2026 The Guard Spec Authors
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#
# Starts Guard Spec on a clean machine with the released images and the full
# detector (L1 rules + L2 classifier + L3 embeddings), or, with
# DETECTOR_LAYERS=l1,l2, in light mode (no L3; less memory, docs/sizing.md):
#
#   1. creates .env from .env.example with strong random secrets (and
#      DETECTOR_LAYERS when it is set), unless .env already exists (it is
#      never overwritten);
#   2. runs `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d` (the released images;
#      not the dev override), whose models-init service pulls and verifies the
#      models before the gateway starts;
#   3. waits for the gateway's /readyz and prints the active layers.
#
# Usage, from the repository root (or a release source archive):
#
#   scripts/quickstart.sh [docker compose options, such as -p myproject]
#
# Environment: DETECTOR_LAYERS (l1,l2 for light mode), GUARDSPEC_VERSION
# (image tag), GATEWAY_PORT and the other
# ports of .env.example, MODELS_MIRROR, COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and
# QUICKSTART_TIMEOUT (seconds to wait for /readyz, default 600). Values set in
# the environment win over .env, as in docker compose.
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

die() {
	echo "quickstart: $*" >&2
	exit 1
}

command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker is not installed"
docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker compose (v2) is not available"
command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "curl is not installed"
[ -f docker-compose.yml ] || die "run this from a Guard Spec checkout (docker-compose.yml not found)"

# rand_hex N: N random bytes as 2N hex characters.
rand_hex() {
	if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		openssl rand -hex "$1"
	else
		od -An -N"$1" -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n'
		echo
	fi
}

# rand_b64 N: N random bytes in base64.
rand_b64() {
	if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		openssl rand -base64 "$1"
	else
		head -c "$1" /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '\n'
		echo
	fi
}

admin_password=""
if [ -f .env ]; then
	echo "quickstart: .env exists, keeping it (delete it to generate new secrets)"
else
	[ -f .env.example ] || die ".env.example not found"
	postgres_password=$(rand_hex 24)
	app_password=$(rand_hex 24)
	jwt_secret=$(rand_hex 32)
	mfa_key=$(rand_b64 32)
	admin_password=$(rand_hex 12)
	for v in "$postgres_password" "$app_password" "$jwt_secret" "$mfa_key" "$admin_password"; do
		[ "${#v}" -ge 24 ] || die "could not generate random secrets (need openssl or /dev/urandom)"
	done
	umask 077
	# Only empty assignments are filled in; GUARD_ENV stays empty (production checks on).
	awk -v pg="$postgres_password" -v app="$app_password" -v jwt="$jwt_secret" \
		-v mfa="$mfa_key" -v admin="$admin_password" -v layers="${DETECTOR_LAYERS:-}" '
		/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$/      { print "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=" pg; next }
		/^GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD=$/ { print "GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD=" app; next }
		/^JWT_SECRET=$/             { print "JWT_SECRET=" jwt; next }
		/^MFA_ENC_KEY=$/            { print "MFA_ENC_KEY=" mfa; next }
		/^ADMIN_PASSWORD=$/         { print "ADMIN_PASSWORD=" admin; next }
		/^DETECTOR_LAYERS=$/        { print "DETECTOR_LAYERS=" layers; next }
		{ print }
	' .env.example >.env.tmp
	for k in POSTGRES_PASSWORD GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD JWT_SECRET MFA_ENC_KEY ADMIN_PASSWORD; do
		grep -q "^$k=..*" .env.tmp || {
			rm -f .env.tmp
			die ".env.example has no empty $k= line to fill in"
		}
	done
	mv .env.tmp .env
	umask 022
	echo "quickstart: wrote .env with new random secrets (mode 600; keep it, back up MFA_ENC_KEY)"
fi

# env_value KEY: the value from the environment, else from .env.
env_value() {
	eval "v=\${$1:-}"
	if [ -z "$v" ]; then
		v=$(sed -n "s/^$1=//p" .env | tail -n 1)
	fi
	printf '%s' "$v"
}

layers=$(env_value DETECTOR_LAYERS | tr -d ' ')
layers=${layers:-l1,l2,l3}
case ",$layers," in
*,l3,*) size="about 270 MB of models" ;;
*,l2,*) size="about 135 MB of models (light mode, no L3)" ;;
label: benign

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright 2026 The Guard Spec Authors
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#
# SSO end-to-end checks against a real identity provider (Keycloak), without
# a browser: curl plays the browser, with a cookie jar per user.
#
#   scripts/sso-e2e.sh          (or: make sso-e2e)
#
# 1. Starts the control plane built from this checkout, Postgres and
#    Keycloak (deploy/compose/sso/compose.yml) as the compose project
#    gs-sso-e2e, on ports of their own, with secrets generated for this run.
# 2. SAML 2.0: creates a SAML provider from Keycloak's IdP metadata, then the
#    matching Keycloak client (its entity id and ACS contain the provider id),
#    maps the Keycloak groups to org roles and runs SP-initiated logins:
#    /start -> Keycloak login form -> credentials -> SAMLResponse -> ACS ->
#    /ui/#/auth/callback?code= -> POST /v1/auth/oidc/exchange -> /v1/auth/me.
#    Negative checks: a replayed SAMLResponse, a response posted without the
#    browser's cookie, an IdP-initiated response while that is off (default),
#    and the replay of an accepted IdP-initiated response once it is allowed.
# 3. OIDC: the same with an OIDC provider and a Keycloak OIDC client.
# 4. SCIM 2.0: an org SCIM token, then an Okta-like sequence with curl
#    (create, get, filter, deactivate, reactivate, group with member, delete),
#    checking memberships, roles and the provisioned user's session.
# 5. Prints PASS / FAIL per check and removes the project (docker compose
#    down -v) unless SSO_E2E_KEEP=1.
#
# Requirements: docker with compose v2, curl, jq, openssl.
#
# Environment (defaults in brackets):
#   SSO_E2E_PROJECT        compose project [gs-sso-e2e]
#   SSO_E2E_CP_PORT        control plane on the host [28081]
#   SSO_E2E_CP_METRICS_PORT control plane metrics [28091]
#   SSO_E2E_PG_PORT        Postgres on the host [25432]
#   SSO_E2E_KC_PORT        Keycloak on the host and its public URL [28180]
#   SSO_E2E_KEEP           1 keeps the stack running afterwards [0]
#   SSO_E2E_NO_BUILD       1 skips building the control plane image [0]
#   SSO_E2E_TIMEOUT        seconds to wait for the services [300]
#
# Every password and key here is a throwaway test value: the Keycloak users'
# passwords are in deploy/compose/sso/realm-guardspec-test.json
# (alice-test-password and so on), the rest is generated for each run.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
ROOT=$(pwd)

PROJECT=${SSO_E2E_PROJECT:-gs-sso-e2e}
CP_PORT=${SSO_E2E_CP_PORT:-28081}
CP_METRICS_PORT=${SSO_E2E_CP_METRICS_PORT:-28091}
PG_PORT=${SSO_E2E_PG_PORT:-25432}
KC_PORT=${SSO_E2E_KC_PORT:-28180}
KEEP=${SSO_E2E_KEEP:-0}
TIMEOUT=${SSO_E2E_TIMEOUT:-300}

CP="http://localhost:$CP_PORT"
KC="http://localhost:$KC_PORT"
REALM=guardspec-test
