# ── Results ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

PASSES=0
FAILS=0
FAILED=""
CODE=000
LOC=""

pass() {
	PASSES=$((PASSES + 1))
	echo "PASS  $*"
}

fail() {
	FAILS=$((FAILS + 1))
	FAILED="$FAILED
  - $*"
	echo "FAIL  $*"
	echo "      last response: HTTP $CODE${LOC:+, Location: $LOC}"
	if [ -s "$W/body" ]; then
		echo "      body: $(head -c 500 "$W/body" | tr '\n' ' ')"
	fi
}

# check DESCRIPTION COMMAND...: PASS when the command succeeds.
check() {
	local desc=$1
	shift
	if "$@"; then
		pass "$desc"
	else
		fail "$desc"
	fi
}

summary() {
	echo
	echo "sso-e2e: $PASSES passed, $FAILS failed"
	if [ "$FAILS" -gt 0 ]; then
		echo "failed checks:$FAILED"
	fi
}

# abort DESCRIPTION: a failed check the rest depends on.
abort() {
	fail "$*"
	summary
	exit 1
}

cleanup() {
	local rc=$?
	if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ -f "$ENVF" ]; then
		echo
		echo "sso-e2e: last control plane and Keycloak log lines:"
		compose logs --no-color --tail 40 control-plane keycloak 2>/dev/null || true
	fi
	if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then
		echo "sso-e2e: SSO_E2E_KEEP=1, the stack keeps running: control plane $CP, Keycloak $KC"
		echo "sso-e2e: test secrets are in $ENVF; remove with: docker compose -p $PROJECT down -v"
	else
		compose down -v --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
		rm -rf "$W"
	fi
	exit "$rc"
}

# ── HTTP helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# req METHOD URL [curl options...]: CODE is the status, the body is in
# $W/body, LOC the Location header. Redirects are never followed.
req() {
	local method=$1 url=$2
	shift 2
	: >"$W/headers"
	CODE=$(curl -sS -X "$method" -o "$W/body" -D "$W/headers" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 30 "$@" "$url") || CODE=000
	LOC=$(sed -n 's/^[Ll]ocation: *//p' "$W/headers" | tr -d '\r' | tail -n 1)
}

api() {

	if [ -n "$data" ]; then
		req "$method" "$CP$path" -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data "$data"

# saml_browser_login USER PASSWORD: SP-initiated login up to the SAMLResponse
# page; the response is saved to $W/saml-USER.*. Uses the jar $W/jar-USER.
saml_browser_login() {
	local user=$1 password=$2 jar="$W/jar-$1"
	req GET "$CP/v1/auth/saml/$SAML_ID/start" -b "$jar" -c "$jar"
	code_is 302 && [[ $LOC == "$KC_REALM/"* ]] || return 1

	req GET "$LOC" -b "$jar" -c "$jar"
	code_is 200 || return 1
	kc_login "$jar" "$user" "$password" || return 1
	code_is 200 || return 1
	saml_extract "$W/saml-$user"
}

saml_login() {
	local user=$1 password=$2
	SESSION_TOKEN=""
	saml_browser_login "$user" "$password" || return 1
	saml_post "$W/jar-$user" "$W/saml-$user"
	code_is 302 || return 1
	local c
	c=$(callback_code) || return 1
	exchange "$c"

#!/bin/sh
# Downloads the native libraries that the `onnx` build tag needs and checks
# their SHA-256 values. Used by build/gateway.Dockerfile and `make onnx-deps`.
#
#   build/onnx-deps.sh <dest-dir> [os] [arch]
#

#                               github.com/daulet/tokenizers (MIT), linked statically
#
# os is linux or darwin, arch is amd64 or arm64 (default: this machine).
#
# ONNX_DEPS_CACHE=<dir> (CI only: a directory restored by actions/cache, or
# mounted into the gateway image build): an archive there named
# <sha256>-<file name> is used instead of the download when its SHA-256
# matches the pin below; otherwise it is downloaded and checked as usual, and
# put there when the directory is writable. Unset (releases), nothing changes.
# Same logic as scripts/fetch-verified.sh, kept here because the Dockerfile
# copies only this file.
set -eu

ORT_VERSION=1.31.1
TOKENIZERS_VERSION=1.27.0

dest=${1:?usage: onnx-deps.sh <dest-dir> [os] [arch]}
os=${2:-$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')}
arch=${3:-$(uname -m)}
case "$arch" in
  x86_64|amd64) arch=amd64 ;;
  aarch64|arm64) arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "unsupported arch: $arch" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

case "$os-$arch" in
  linux-amd64)
    ort_pkg=onnxruntime-linux-x64-$ORT_VERSION
    ort_sha=c849e36a1ef3e22d4ff217b9d1ce4a3cf5b9467b975610913ae959ad5b16bdc9
    tok_sha=72556cdca798dd4ea7cdaba308e5f0d68a8cb93b67c96edf485b7a0edd7b07f4 ;;
  linux-arm64)
    ort_pkg=onnxruntime-linux-aarch64-$ORT_VERSION
    ort_sha=5317505e2da99be65f8e2775ba3c2afd6d2961fd78aba1bd8f56159f48820c78
    tok_sha=e96545ad05930c26f51f63d932ee6d3bbd32bbed149e102c5290d587a2293067 ;;
  darwin-arm64)
    ort_pkg=onnxruntime-osx-arm64-$ORT_VERSION
    ort_sha=2e1344a1926ee50eb25b38153cb6992c3567515aef0e677a1a520a1798896d6f
    tok_sha=fb84b8b2e349a5952767ffe80ccd862fc44084de47f3b0cc3f0b7c9d4e649cf7 ;;
  *) echo "unsupported platform: $os-$arch" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

sha256() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
  else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

fetch() { # url sha256 out
  if [ -n "${ONNX_DEPS_CACHE:-}" ]; then
    cached=$ONNX_DEPS_CACHE/$2-${1##*/}
    if [ -f "$cached" ]; then
      cp "$cached" "$3"
      if [ "$(sha256 "$3")" = "$2" ]; then
        echo "${1##*/} from $ONNX_DEPS_CACHE, sha256 ok"
        return 0
      fi
      echo "ignoring $cached: sha256 mismatch" >&2
      rm -f "$3"
    fi
  fi
  # A release download hit four 504s in 7 s (v0.1.0-rc.3): retry for longer.
  curl -fsSL --retry 6 --retry-delay 10 --retry-max-time 300 -o "$3" "$1"
  got=$(sha256 "$3")

    echo "sha256 mismatch for $1: got $got, want $2" >&2
    rm -f "$3"; exit 1

  if [ -n "${ONNX_DEPS_CACHE:-}" ]; then
    { mkdir -p "$ONNX_DEPS_CACHE" && cp "$3" "$ONNX_DEPS_CACHE/$2-${1##*/}"; } 2>/dev/null || true
  fi

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

fetch "https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/download/v$ORT_VERSION/$ort_pkg.tgz" "$ort_sha" "$tmp/ort.tgz"

case "$os" in

# Installs the pinned Trivy release for CI (.github/workflows/vuln-scan.yml)

# archive. The pin was checked against Trivy's signed checksums with
#   cosign verify-blob --bundle trivy_<v>_checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
#     --certificate-identity https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/.github/workflows/reusable-release.yaml@refs/tags/v<v> \
#     --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com trivy_<v>_checksums.txt
# Update VERSION and SHA256 together (linux amd64), after the same check, and
# prefer a release that is at least two weeks old.
#
# DOWNLOAD_CACHE=<dir>: take the archive from that directory (CI's
# actions/cache) when it has the pinned SHA-256; see scripts/fetch-verified.sh.
set -eu

VERSION=0.76.1
SHA256=c7cbe3137fb8a48a17574bede3dd6beb16742d1e9772929940fc90082c39d9c0

dir=${1:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-.}/bin}
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
archive="trivy_${VERSION}_Linux-64bit.tar.gz"
sh "$(dirname "$0")/fetch-verified.sh" \
  "https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/download/v${VERSION}/${archive}" "$SHA256" "$tmp/$archive"
echo "$SHA256  $tmp/$archive" | sha256sum -c -
mkdir -p "$dir"
tar -xzf "$tmp/$archive" -C "$tmp" trivy
install -m 0755 "$tmp/trivy" "$dir/trivy"
"$dir/trivy" --version

#!/bin/sh
# Copyright 2026 The Guard Spec Authors
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#
# Restores a backup of scripts/backup.sh into a compose stack whose database
# is empty: a new host, a new compose project, or the same project after
# `docker compose down -v`. It never overwrites a database that has tables.
#
# Usage:
#
#   scripts/restore.sh [-f compose file] [-p project] [-e env file] BACKUP_DIR
#
#   -f, -p, -e  as in scripts/backup.sh. When the env file does not exist,
#               the backup's guardspec.env is copied there (mode 600); when
#               it exists, its MFA_ENC_KEY must match the backup's (set
#               RESTORE_ALLOW_KEY_CHANGE=1 to restore anyway: every user's
#               2FA then has to be reset).
#
# Steps: verify the dump's sha256 against MANIFEST; start postgres; refuse a
# non-empty database; create the cluster-wide role guardspec_app (pg_dump
# does not carry roles); pg_restore; restore Caddy's /data when the backup and
# the stack have it; then `docker compose up -d --wait`, whose migrate and
# db-roles jobs apply newer migrations, if any, and set the guardspec_app
# password from the env file.
#
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # $POSTGRES_DB and $1 in single quotes expand in the container
set -eu

root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
file=$root/docker-compose.yml
project=
envfile=

die() {
	echo "restore: $*" >&2
	exit 1
}

while getopts f:p:e:h opt; do
	case $opt in
	f) file=$OPTARG ;;
	p) project=$OPTARG ;;
	e) envfile=$OPTARG ;;
	*)
		sed -n '4,/^set -eu/p' "$0" | grep -v '^# shellcheck\|^set -eu' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
		exit 2
		;;
	esac
done
shift $((OPTIND - 1))

# ==> scripts/fetch-verified.sh <==
#!/bin/sh
# Copyright 2026 The Guard Spec Authors
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#
# Downloads URL to OUT and checks its SHA-256; on a mismatch OUT is removed
# and the script fails. Used by CI for pinned tool downloads.
#
#   scripts/fetch-verified.sh <url> <sha256> <out>
#
# DOWNLOAD_CACHE=<dir> (CI: a directory restored by actions/cache): a file
# there named <sha256>-<basename of url> is copied to OUT instead of
# downloading, and kept only when the copy has the pinned SHA-256; otherwise
# the URL is downloaded as usual and the verified file is put in the cache
# for the next run. A cache entry can save a download, never skip the check.
set -eu

usage='usage: fetch-verified.sh <url> <sha256> <out>'
url=${1:?$usage}
want=${2:?$usage}
out=${3:?$usage}

sha256() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
  else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

cached=
if [ -n "${DOWNLOAD_CACHE:-}" ]; then
  cached=$DOWNLOAD_CACHE/$want-${url##*/}
  if [ -f "$cached" ]; then
    cp "$cached" "$out"
    if [ "$(sha256 "$out")" = "$want" ]; then
      echo "fetch-verified: ${url##*/} from the cache, sha256 ok"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "fetch-verified: ignoring $cached: sha256 mismatch" >&2
    rm -f "$out" "$cached"
  fi
fi

# GitHub Releases answered 504 for hours on 2026-11-09: retry for up to 5
# minutes, on any error, before failing (the cache covers longer outages).
curl -fsSL --retry 8 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-max-time 300 -o "$out" "$url"
got=$(sha256 "$out")
if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
  echo "fetch-verified: sha256 mismatch for $url: got $got, want $want" >&2
  rm -f "$out"
  exit 1
fi
echo "fetch-verified: ${url##*/} downloaded, sha256 ok"
if [ -n "$cached" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$DOWNLOAD_CACHE"
  cp "$out" "$cached"
fi

# ==> deploy/postgres/set-app-password.sh <==
#!/bin/sh
# Sets the password of the application role guardspec_app from
# GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD. Run it after the migrations, with
# superuser credentials in the libpq environment (PGHOST, PGUSER, PGDATABASE,
# PGPASSWORD). It is idempotent, so it also rotates the password.
#
# Outside development (GUARD_ENV other than "dev") it refuses known default or
# short passwords for both the superuser and guardspec_app.
set -eu

min_len=12

lower() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }

# weak VALUE: true when VALUE is a known default or shorter than min_len.
weak() {
	case "$(lower "$1")" in
	ps | guardspec_app | postgres | password | secret | changeme | change-me | admin | \
		guardspec | test | dev | change-me-in-production | dev-only-*)
		return 0 ;;
	esac
	[ "${#1}" -lt "$min_len" ]
}

if [ -z "${GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
	echo "GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD is not set; set GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD to a unique password of at least $min_len characters (see .env.example)" >&2
	exit 1
fi

if [ "$(lower "${GUARD_ENV:-}")" != "dev" ]; then
	failed=0
	if weak "${PGPASSWORD:-}"; then
		echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD is a known default or shorter than $min_len characters; set POSTGRES_PASSWORD to a unique password (see .env.example), or GUARD_ENV=dev for local development" >&2
		failed=1
	fi
	if weak "$GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD"; then
		echo "GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD is a known default or shorter than $min_len characters; set GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD to a unique password (see .env.example), or GUARD_ENV=dev for local development" >&2
		failed=1
	fi
	[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
fi

# The password goes in as a psql variable, quoted by psql, never spliced into SQL.
psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -v app_password="$GUARDSPEC_APP_PASSWORD" <<'SQL'
ALTER ROLE guardspec_app WITH PASSWORD :'app_password';
SQL
echo "guardspec_app password set"

text:
+-- TOTP (RFC 6238). Secrets are AES-GCM ciphertexts (MFA_ENC_KEY, the user id
+-- as additional data). pending_secret_enc is a setup not yet confirmed;
+-- last_used_step refuses a code a second time within its window.
+CREATE TABLE user_mfa (
+    user_id            UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    totp_secret_enc    BYTEA,
+    pending_secret_enc BYTEA,
+    enabled_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
+    last_used_step     BIGINT,
+    updated_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
+);
+
+CREATE TABLE mfa_recovery_codes (
+    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    code_hash  TEXT NOT NULL,
+    used_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
+    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
+);
+CREATE INDEX idx_mfa_recovery_codes_user ON mfa_recovery_codes (user_id);
+
+-- The second step of a login (the mfa_token, a 5-minute JWT whose jti is the
+-- id): purpose verify asks for a code, enroll for a 2FA setup. Each allows 5
+-- attempts and one success.
+CREATE TABLE mfa_challenges (
+    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
+    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    purpose    TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT mfa_challenges_purpose CHECK (purpose IN ('verify', 'enroll')),
+    method     TEXT NOT NULL,
+    attempts   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    used_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
+    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
+    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
+);
+CREATE INDEX idx_mfa_challenges_expires ON mfa_challenges (expires_at);
+
+-- Per-organization login rules. No row: the defaults (no 2FA requirement,
+-- every login method, 12-hour sessions). allowed_login_methods NULL allows all.
+CREATE TABLE org_security (
+    org_id                 UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    require_mfa            BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
+    sso_satisfies_mfa      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
+    allowed_login_methods  TEXT[],
+    domain_join            JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
+    session_lifetime_hours INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 12
+        CONSTRAINT org_security_session_lifetime CHECK (session_lifetime_hours BETWEEN 1 AND 12),
+    updated_at             TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
+);
+ALTER TABLE org_security ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_org_security ON org_security
+    USING (org_id = current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid);
+
+-- Admin actions. org_id NULL is an instance-level row (SSO providers, instance
+-- users, logins), visible only in a transaction that sets app.instance_scope,
+-- which the control plane does for instance administrators.
+CREATE TABLE activity_log (
+    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+    org_id      UUID REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
+    actor_id    UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
+    actor_email TEXT,
+    action      TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT activity_log_action CHECK (char_length(action) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
+    target      TEXT CONSTRAINT activity_log_target CHECK (char_length(target) <= 512),
+    ip          TEXT CONSTRAINT activity_log_ip CHECK (char_length(ip) <= 64),
+    details     JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
+);
+CREATE INDEX idx_activity_log_org ON activity_log (org_id, at DESC, id DESC);
+ALTER TABLE activity_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_activity ON activity_log
+    USING (org_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.org_id', true), '')::uuid);
+CREATE POLICY instance_activity ON activity_log
+    USING (org_id IS NULL AND current_setting('app.instance_scope', true) = 'on');
+
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON sessions, identity_providers, user_identities, oidc_states, oidc_codes,
+    user_mfa, mfa_recovery_codes, mfa_challenges, org_security, activity_log TO guardspec_app;
+
+-- The login rules of every organization a user belongs to, read at login
+-- before any organization is chosen. Runs with the owner's rights, like
+-- user_organizations (012); returns only the given user's organizations.
+CREATE FUNCTION user_org_security(uid UUID)
+RETURNS TABLE (org_id UUID, require_mfa BOOLEAN, sso_satisfies_mfa BOOLEAN)
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp
+AS $$
+    SELECT m.org_id, COALESCE(s.require_mfa, false), COALESCE(s.sso_satisfies_mfa, false)
+    FROM org_memberships m
+    LEFT JOIN org_security s ON s.org_id = m.org_id
+    WHERE m.user_id = uid
+$$;
+REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION user_org_security(UUID) FROM PUBLIC;
+GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION user_org_security(UUID) TO guardspec_app;
+
+-- The organizations whose domain_join rule matches an SSO login (verified
+-- email domain and provider), with the role to grant.
+CREATE FUNCTION domain_join_orgs(dom TEXT, provider UUID)
+RETURNS TABLE (org_id UUID, role org_role)
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp
+AS $$
+    SELECT s.org_id, (r->>'role')::org_role
+    FROM org_security s, jsonb_array_elements(s.domain_join) r
+    WHERE lower(r->>'domain') = lower(dom)
+      AND (r->>'provider_id')::uuid = provider
+      AND r->>'role' IN ('viewer', 'member', 'admin')
+$$;
+REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION domain_join_orgs(TEXT, UUID) FROM PUBLIC;
+GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION domain_join_orgs(TEXT, UUID) TO guardspec_app;

+name: Examples
+

+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - "examples/**"
+      - "cmd/gateway/**"
+      - "internal/**"
+      - "migrations/**"
+      - "docker-compose*.yml"
+      - "go.mod"
+      - "go.sum"
+      - ".github/workflows/examples.yml"
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    paths:
+      - "examples/**"
+      - "cmd/gateway/**"
+      - "internal/**"
+      - "migrations/**"
+      - "docker-compose*.yml"
+      - "go.mod"
+      - "go.sum"

+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: examples-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true

+jobs:
+  examples:
+    name: Run the examples (Python, TypeScript, n8n shape)

+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    env:
